REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  MEETING
  MINUTES
  JUNE 28, 2021

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.
.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Silvano, Shinn, Ciarolla, Robinson, Griggs, Harik, Brtis, Nilsen

Committee Members Absent:  Martin, Zigrang

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor, Cynthia Morquecho

DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 24, 2021

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS, to:

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE MAY 24, 2021, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF so ordered.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

None.

STAFF ITEMS

  A. COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis stated that events are back to normal and that restrictions only apply to mega events
with a size of 10,000 or more attendees and most of our events are no more than 5,000. City
Celebration subcommittee will be convening soon. Face coverings are not required outdoors for
vaccinated and non-vaccinated people. City facilities will require face coverings for non-
vaccinated people indoors. Meetings can happen in person indoors but non-vaccinated people
will need to wear a mask. It will be up to the Committee to decide how to meet.

Council Member Huff asked if a hybrid in person and Zoom meeting could be made. ACM Davis
responded that the City was not equipped technically for hybrid meetings just yet due to
equipment being back ordered. The Committee could continue to meet virtually.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  1
JUNE 28, 2021
 The issue of feedback during live streaming is an issue staff is working on. Staff expects a Fall
delivery of equipment. Committee Member Silvano stated she did not mind meeting in person.
ACM Davis noted that if in person was preferred by the Committee and will plan for that next
meeting. Committee Member Robinson asked if people could still call in. ACM Davis responded
that the call-in option would not be available if we were to meet in-person due to the technical
constraints.

  B. PROPOSAL FOR NEW EQUESTRIAN AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief review of the staff report. Committee Member Robinson
noted the idea came from Sacramento Folsom Lake Trails where a similar program is installed.
A pair of riders in identifying t-shirts would visit parks and help visitors become familiar with the
trails and pointing out trail violations such as bikes. George F Canyon trail walkers would benefit
from seeing horses and to learn about horse trail etiquette.

Committee Member Silvano suggested the program should be separate from the Equestrian
Committee. Committee Member Robinson noted the program would be volunteer based.
Committee Member Harik added the Committee is limited in numbers but supports a separate
program. Committee Member Shinn notes concerns related to the Brown Act if the Committee
served in this capacity and that committee members could be faced with confrontational situations
and that she prefers the volunteer aspect of the program. Committee Member Harik noted it was
great community outreach. Committee Member Robinson would like to apply this program to
George F Canyon since many people are not familiar with horses in the area, there are plans to
remodel the nature enter, a talk about the equestrian community can be had there when finished.

It was further discussed that the City Celebration can also be an event where the ambassadors
can attend to show children interest in horses, which can cultivate future horse riders.
Committee Member Robinson responded that the riders will not be confrontational and just be
available for public information. Committee Member Shinn asked if riders should be trained and
that the program should have rules and regulations for it.

ACM Davis noted a small subcommittee could be formed to develop a concept to be reviwed by
the Committee and brought to the Parks & Activities Commission and then City Council for
approval. Committee Members Robinson and Harik volunteered.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF so ordered.

  C. FOURTH OF JULY SAFETY UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis noted the community concern brought to City staff over fire safety during the holiday
with actions the City plans: Sheriff’s Posse will patrol the trails; Landfill closure will be closed early
at 7p.m. four days before and after the holiday. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith added
that Peter Weber Equestrian Center was given the City notice which was sent to boarders and
pubic messages have been sent through NIXLE as well.

Firework prevention was posted on social media along with PSAs from the Mayor and
surrounding cities. The school district will close their gates at Rancho Vista and may increase
their security.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  2
JUNE 28, 2021
 Council Member Huff asked if the Sheriffs were tracking fireworks violators throughout the City
or just the landfill area. ACM Davis responded that the Sheriff Department will respond to calls
but in regards to prevention, the Sheriffs are looking for groups of people and asking them what
their purpose on the trail was. Council Member Huff asked about a policy on 4th of July parties.
ACM Davis stated no restrictions on block parties and that the City be contacted in advance so
that emergency services could navigate access points if needed.

  D. ENFORCEMENT ON TRAILS AND ARENAS (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho stated that the recent uptick in bikes, specifically e-bikes and strollers on
the trails, and off-leash dogs in park areas has prompted the City Community Services Code
Compliance Officer to increase patrols of all parks and will include random Saturdays to enforce
trail and park regulations. The Sheriff’s Department is also available to reach out to for
enforcement issues.

Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that signage is at all trail entrances and key
areas. ACM Davis noted the increase in signage at the beginning of 2020 and shared that other
cities are seeing increases in outdoor participants at their facilities which may decrease after
Summer.

Council Member Huff asked if a reminder could be posted on newsletters and that rider safety
could be promoted as the main focal point of enforcing guidelines. Committee Member Robinson
asked if a notice could be posted on the website as well. Committee Member Griggs noted most
violators are from out of town and that information could be posted on the sites they download
their trail guides. Committee Member Robinson noted the trail sign typically gets knocked over.
Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith notes some bicyclists pick up the sign and set them
aside. Staff is doing all they can and have also reached out to the Sheriffs. ACM Davis noted
the regulations are periodically posted on social media. Committee Member Ciarolla asked if
there is any ordinance on trail regulations. ACM Davis affirmed and also noted it may be a part
of Park Regulations.

Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the trail crossing between the Botanic Garden and
Church parking lot being used for pedestrians when the Gardens has events. Staff has been
posting signs when notified but it is at a cost of staff time and resources, thus it was requested
that this be requested of the Garden directly. Committee Member Harik stated the signage is
overkill. Committee Member Silvano asked if a NIXLE post could be sent out. Maintenance
Superintendent Goldsmith responded that the signage would not be necessary to post every time
as it is little impact and most trail users know the area. Committee Member Shinn asked if a
permanent sign could be posted to satisfy all parties. Committee Member Brtis asked who had
the key to the gate. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that the Botanic Garden
had the key. Committee Members Brtis and Shinn stated that whoever has the keys should put
the sign up. Committee Member Harik agreed with the permanent sign option. Committee
Member Brtis noted that pedestrians do not pay attention to their surroundings or horses when
passing and come along with strollers at times. Committee Member Harik noted putting a sign
on the other side noting the horse crossing for pedestrians would be a good idea as well.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  3
JUNE 28, 2021
   E. EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

ACM Davis stated the trail riding operation from the May Committee meeting has obtained the
necessary license and permit. The City is looking into streamline the process for trail riding
businesses and may be coming back with consistent rules and guidelines for a Municipal Update
and may add an additional line for horse trail riding businesses and their fees. Council Member
Huff noted that the business owner was very willing to work with nearby residents near his
business. Staff hopes to continue discussions with residents concerned with his business.
Committee Member Harik noted the business had two strings of riders when observing the trails
during a horse show at Ernie Howlett park. ACM Davis noted the City Manager had written a
letter to Palos Verdes Estates with itemized concerns. Council Member Huff noted the City of
Palos Verdes Estates did address some of the issues and may be addressed if there are further
complaints.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  F. MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho requested that the Committee help to get the word
out and to the equestrian community about the upcoming event and noted an RSVP system is in
place for riders wanting a breakfast. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the difficulty
of getting students riding in the event due to Summer break but will attend the event himself.
ACM Davis noted six City riders and dignitaries confirmed to date. This would be the City’s first
large outdoor event since the pandemic. Council Member Huff asked about the Scouts not
attending the breakfast. Community Services Supervisor Morquecho responded that the Scouts
were not available to prepare and serve breakfast due to the schedule but are expected to come
back in the future now that COVID restrictions have lifted. Committee Member Robinson asked
if breakfast attendees had to ride. Community Services Supervisor Morquecho responded that
they could just meet at the park to attend the breakfast. Council Member Huff asked if there was
another event at Chandler Park. ACM Davis noted that Chandler Park was where the ride begins,
ending at Ernie Howlett Park. Council Member Huff asked what food would be served. ACM
Davis said a breakfast has not been finalized but will be a grab and go option from a local
business. Committee Member Shinn asked if a carriage will be used this year. ACM Davis said
that no carriages will be on the trail.

Council Member Huff noted the Community Services Supervisor Morquecho will be leaving the
City of Rolling Hills Estates for another City closer to her home. Community Services Supervisor
Morquecho expressed her gratitude for the two years working for this RHE.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A. ADOPT-A- TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

None.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  4
JUNE 28, 2021
   A. JULY COMMITTEE MEETING POSTPONEMENT AND CITY CELEBRATION

ACM Davis suggested that since Community Services Supervisor Morquecho will not be available
in July and the City Celebration Subcommittee will be meeting then, that the Committee not meet
in July but convene in August for the next meeting with an update on the City Celebration. Council
Member Huff noted that if something came up in between, a meeting could be scheduled.
Committee Member Harik asked when the City Celebration was scheduled. ACM Davis
responded September 25th at the Empty Saddle Club. Community Services Supervisor
Morquecho noted we are still awaiting a response from the Empty Saddle Club. Committee
Member Harik noted how her horse trainer was impressed by the past City Celebration events.
Council Member Huff noted that Ernie Howlett was too spread out. Maintenance Superintendent
Goldsmith noted the Empty Saddle Club provided a better rustic western vibe for the event.
Committee Member Harik noted a successful horse show.

ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR HUFF ADJOURNED THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING 8:00 pm

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

___________________________
Daniel A-Haja  __________________________
Community Services Coordinator  Britt Huff, Chair

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  5
JUNE 28, 2021
